title: Should streaming pay artists differently?

turns.speaker: Esme
turns.text: My band got about nine pounds for eleven thousand streams last month. I checked it twice because I assumed I'd misread it.

turns.speaker: Vik
turns.text: That's roughly the going rate. The per-stream number is somewhere under a third of a penny once the label takes its share.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: The part most people don't know is how the pot is divided. All the subscription money goes into one pool and gets split by total share of plays.

turns.speaker: Esme
turns.text: So my subscription doesn't go to the people I listen to.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Almost none of it. If you only played your band all month, most of your ten pounds still goes to whoever is globally biggest.

turns.speaker: Vik
turns.text: User-centric payment fixes exactly that, and it's been trialled. Your money follows your listening.

turns.speaker: Vik
turns.text: Small artists gain, the very biggest lose a little, and that's why it moves slowly.

turns.speaker: Esme
turns.text: How much do small artists gain?

turns.speaker: Vik
turns.text: Less than people hope. It's a better model, not a solution. The pool is still small.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Which is the real issue. Recorded music got much cheaper for listeners and nobody wants to reverse that.

turns.speaker: Esme
turns.text: I don't either, honestly. I listen to more music than I could ever have bought.

turns.speaker: Vik
turns.text: So the income moved to touring and merchandise, which favours whoever can afford to tour.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Meaning the model quietly selects for people with money behind them already.

points: A band received about nine pounds for eleven thousand streams, reflecting a per-stream rate under a third of a penny.
Subscription revenue is pooled and divided by global share of plays, so a listener's money largely does not reach the artists they play.
User-centric payment models redirect each subscription to that listener's artists and have been trialled.
Vik cautions the gain for small artists is modest, since the total pool remains small.
Tariq notes recorded music became much cheaper for listeners, which nobody wishes to reverse.
Income has shifted to touring and merchandise, which favours artists who can already afford to tour.
